title: sensor-source-ref-episode-drift.json re-run a later night against the same committed record it was proposed against, confirms unchanged, and is promoted; the practice's two other PROPOSED sensors are checked and still not promotable
statement: foreknown/proposals/sensor-source-ref-episode-drift.json was written 2026-09-18 (obs-2026-09-18-1.json) with a mechanical, stateless test_rule and no threshold: it already reported 10 confirmed instances the night it was proposed. No foreknown notary run has posted for 2026-09-19 as of this pass (newest committed foreknown/snapshots/<date>/ is still 2026-09-18; autonomy/log.jsonl's newest foreknown-notary-run entry is dated 2026-09-18T10:02:37+00:00, and tonight's registry-stall-check at 2026-09-19T05:36:09+00:00 reports stale: [] -- the record simply has not moved since, not a gap). Re-running the test_rule directly against foreknown/registry.json (current) and foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-18/gdacs.json (newest preserved) reproduces the identical 10 futures, stored/current episode pairs and gaps obs-2026-09-18-1.json reported: gdacs-tc-1001305 (15->47), gdacs-fl-1104121 (2->14), gdacs-fl-1104081 (7->18), gdacs-tc-1001297 (51->55), gdacs-dr-1018332 (18->21), gdacs-dr-1018431 (11->14), gdacs-dr-1027450 (5->8), gdacs-dr-1027465 (2->5), gdacs-dr-1027449 (6->8), gdacs-wf-1030252 (39->40). Neither falsification condition named in the proposal has occurred: futures.py's TRACKED_FIELDS still excludes source_ref, and no maintainer note declares source_ref a permanent first-episode anchor. Under the standing delegation (docs/2026-08-12-promotion-authority.md), a mechanical test_rule with no wait condition that already held the night it was proposed and holds again on a later night is promotable; promoted tonight as practice/src/practice/foreknown/futures.py's source_ref_episode_drift(), wired into run.py (field source_ref_episode_drift in run.json, count in the autonomy detail) and unit-tested against fixed fixtures covering drift, no-drift, and the unrevised/closed/non-GDACS exclusions the definition and falsification clause both name, so the check does not depend on tonight's data staying frozen to keep passing. Checked the practice's two remaining PROPOSED sensors against the current record: sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json's only live case, gdacs-tc-1001305, is still OPEN with no closure event since its 2026-08-28 REAPPEARED (registry history unchanged since a REVISED on 2026-09-03) -- a full scan of every future with a REAPPEARED event in its history finds no second case either, so the sensor's test_rule has still not fired and it is not promotable. sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json's review chain is unchanged: gdacs-fl-1103815's datemodified reads the identical 2026-09-03T13:36:40 across all four newly-available nights since its last review (2026-09-15 through 2026-09-18), extending its frozen run to 16 nights without breaking lockstep a second time, and the design problem its 2026-09-18 review left open (separating a shared-timestamp batch touch from a genuine per-record freeze) is unaddressed by this pass.
method: Confirmed no new foreknown snapshot exists for 2026-09-19 (ls foreknown/snapshots; newest is 2026-09-18) and that this is an ordinary gap, not a stall (autonomy/log.jsonl's registry-stall-check entry at 2026-09-19T05:36:09+00:00 reports stale: []). Loaded foreknown/registry.json and foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-18/gdacs.json and recomputed sensor-source-ref-episode-drift.json's test_rule by hand (regex-extracting episodeid/eventid from each OPEN, >=1-REVISED GDACS future's stored source_ref and comparing against properties.episodeid for the matching properties.eventid in the newest snapshot's features), reproducing all 10 instances and gaps obs-2026-09-18-1.json reported, byte-identical. Read practice/src/practice/foreknown/futures.py's TRACKED_FIELDS and update_registry() in full to confirm neither falsification condition has been met. Implemented source_ref_episode_drift(registry, gdacs_feed) in futures.py (regex-based, scoped to OPEN GDACS futures with >=1 REVISED event, matched on properties.eventid), wired it into run.py as a new source_ref_episode_drift field in run.json and a count in the autonomy-log detail, following the same per-run-block pattern as the already-promoted primary_iso3_dropped and drought_window_crossings checks. Added three tests to practice/tests/test_foreknown.py: a drifted case (matches the gdacs-tc-1001305 numbers), a no-drift control (matches the gdacs-fl-1104124 shape from the proposal), and an exclusions case (unrevised, CLOSED_BY_SOURCE, and non-GDACS futures all produce no finding). Updated sensor-source-ref-episode-drift.json's status to PROMOTED with a promotion block naming the implementation, the re-run evidence and what stayed unchanged. Scanned foreknown/registry.json for every future with a REAPPEARED event in its history (one: gdacs-tc-1001305) and counted CLOSED_BY_SOURCE/DISSIPATED events after that REAPPEARED timestamp (zero) to re-check sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json. Read properties.datemodified for gdacs-fl-1103815 from foreknown/snapshots/2026-09-15/gdacs.json through 2026-09-18/gdacs.json to extend sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json's frozen-run count. Read memoryhole/readings/2026-09-17.json (the newest reading) in full: zero entries[].abstentions across all 54 entries, so no verdicts file is due tonight. Ran python -m pip install -e ./practice, python -m pytest practice/tests (185 passed, up from 182), python stage/generate.py --repo-root . and python verify.py --repo-root . after writing all changes; all green.
worth_watching_because: This is the practice's first sensor promotion since sensor-registry-stall.json (2026-09-07) and the first to promote against a record that had not moved between the proposal night and the promotion night -- the proposal's own test_rule already anticipated this ("no threshold or multiple-night wait is needed"), and re-running it by hand rather than trusting yesterday's own count is what tonight's pass adds: the same 10 futures, the same gaps, confirmed independently rather than copied forward. Once GDACS moves any of these events another episode further, or the notary posts a 2026-09-19 run, source_ref_episode_drift will report against fresh bytes and the promoted test is already shaped to keep tracking it without another promotion.
left_alone: Not widening sensor-source-ref-episode-drift's scope to NHC or NWS futures: its own falsification clause already scopes it to GDACS only (NHC's source_ref is a fixed constant; NWS's is a CAP @id this observatory has not confirmed does or does not change on revision), and nothing this pass found argues for revisiting that scope. Not attempting sensor-source-reconfirmation-blind-spot.json's open redesign problem (separating a shared-timestamp batch touch from a genuine per-record datemodified freeze) -- four more frozen nights for gdacs-fl-1103815 extend the same evidence its 2026-09-18 review already has, not a new finding. Not promoting sensor-resolution-reappearance-coverage.json: its only live case has still not closed a second time, so its test_rule has not fired, the same state every prior pass has found since 2026-08-30. No memoryhole verdicts written: the newest reading (2026-09-17) carries zero rule-layer abstentions. darkocean's dma sub-source outage continues (autonomy/log.jsonl, 2026-09-18T09:14:07+00:00, "dma": "outage: URLError"); already covered by obs-2026-08-13-2.json and obs-2026-08-22-1.json and unchanged in shape, so not re-reported.
